text: Confirmed 2026-11-16: from GitHub Actions, requests for FDA summary PDFs and even the FDA record page are redirected by FDA's bot-defence service (AkamaiGHost) to an abuse-detection page, with the project's honest user agent and 30 second pacing. The address itself is correct. FDA offers no official bulk route to summary text: openFDA and the downloadable 510(k) files carry metadata only. Automated reading is switched off while the probe sees this, it is not worked around, and document-verified labels come only from manual reviews. The probe re-checks once a day and reading resumes by itself if access opens.

FDA's comparison table lists computer vision and machine-learning-based algorithms, and the extracted text does not show which device each belongs to. The AI-assisted label is supported; the method is not settled. Quotes and page numbers are not yet compared with the PDF by a person.

FDA's robots.txt asks for 30 seconds between requests, which the reader now follows, and names visiting hours of 23:00 to 05:00 Eastern. The daily run is at 11:17 UTC, outside those hours. The file lists no disallow rule for /cdrh_docs/.

An outside fetch of the public files returned an older version. GitHub Pages and the raw file host cache for several minutes. Each output now carries a build stamp and a content id, and a workflow job compares the live files with the built ones after every run.
Analysis exists for four stories, all written by Claude and none independently reviewed.
FDA applicant IDs are name slugs, so spelling variants can split one company. The same company is not linked across FDA and SEC.
Deadlines adjust for weekends, not federal holidays, so a filing one business day over may be on time.
Significant-modification analysis is not built. Only same-company reference devices and change-control-plan mentions are flagged.
